gloss: postdating; advance dating; appetizer; first course (in kaiseki cuisine)

definitions.explanation: Writing a future date on a document, check, or other item, so that it becomes effective at that later date.
The opening dish served at the beginning of a kaiseki or traditional Japanese multi-course meal, typically a small, seasonal appetizer.

examples.japanese: {小切手|こぎって}を{先付|さきづ}けで{切|き}った。
examples.english: I wrote the check with a future date.

examples.japanese: {先付|さきづ}けの{領収書|りょうしゅうしょ}は{受|う}け{付|つ}けられない。
examples.english: A postdated receipt will not be accepted.

examples.japanese: {先付|さきづ}けにすることで、{支払|しはら}い{日|び}を{先|さき}に{延|の}ばすことができる。
examples.english: By postdating, you can push the payment date further out.

examples.japanese: {先付|さきづ}けは{季節|きせつ}の{食材|しょくざい}を{使|つか}った{小鉢|こばち}だった。
examples.english: The appetizer was a small dish using seasonal ingredients.

examples.japanese: {懐石料理|かいせきりょうり}の{先付|さきづ}けには{旬|しゅん}の{味|あじ}が{凝縮|ぎょうしゅく}されている。
examples.english: The appetizer course of kaiseki cuisine captures the essence of the season.

examples.japanese: コースが{始|はじ}まり、まず{先付|さきづ}けとして{豆腐|とうふ}の{上|うえ}に{梅|うめ}ソースを{添|そ}えた{一品|いっぴん}が{出|で}てきた。
examples.english: The course began, and first, as an appetizer, a dish of tofu topped with plum sauce was served.

notes:
Two distinct meanings sharing the same word.

SENSE 1 (postdating): Formed from {先|さき} (ahead/future) and {付|つ}ける (to attach/put). Refers to marking a document with a date in the future. Common in business and financial contexts.

SENSE 2 (kaiseki appetizer): In {懐石料理|かいせきりょうり} (kaiseki cuisine), the {先付|さきづ}け is the opening course, served before everything else. It sets the tone and showcases the season's flavors. The name literally means "served first." This sense is also written as {先附|さきづ}け.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {先付|さきづ}けの{小切手|こぎって}: postdated check
- {先付|さきづ}けの{小鉢|こばち}: appetizer small bowl

RELATED TERMS:
- {日付|ひづけ}: date
- {懐石料理|かいせきりょうり}: kaiseki cuisine
- {前菜|ぜんさい}: appetizer; hors d'oeuvres (Western-style)
- {八寸|はっすん}: assorted appetizer plate (another kaiseki course)
